steps.message:
Gordon, Bianca at Ocotillo wants a straight answer on whether the E119 companion simulation validated, for the launch materials. I can't close my review of the Phase 1 draft until section 7 exists, so I need the validation memo from you.

Work from the companion run as it stands, the appropriate test report and certification document, the amended numbers Bianca sent over, and the dimensioned assembly drawing. Our own procedure governs how the result gets reported. No new runs or tests are available and nothing is being asked of Red Butte or Ironwood, so this comes out of what is on the file server today, 10/10/2025, and nothing else on it needs changing.

Settle whether the assembly in the run is the one the certification covers and tell me what that rests on. I need the governing criterion and the time it is reached, and I need to know whether the prediction in the section 7 stub stands. I need the experimental value you adopt and your disposition on Bianca's figure. On the strength of those I need the error, the acceptance criterion, the uncertainty, and how the error compares against both. I also want the largest prediction that would have cleared the criterion.

Two comparisons belong in the memo as well: the minutes separating the two criteria in the test against the same separation in the run, and how far the governing point sits above the nine point mean at governance in each. Tell me what they say about the model, where the rework belongs, and whether any of that rework has been started yet. I also need what all of this means for the rest of Phase 1.

The memo also needs what this exercise does and does not establish about Ocotillo's wildfire claim and what would close that gap, including the form any future comparison would have to be reported in. I need what Bianca's figure would do to the certified rating if it were ever substantiated and who is entitled to act on that, the stamp language, and my checklist disposition: which item the memo lets me close and which of the rest stay open. Give it to me as a Word memo with crossing times rather than the samples that trip them, times to the nearest minute, limits as they fall, and every number carrying its unit. Add a short paragraph I can send Bianca today.

## Where to put your answer

Save the files that make up your answer under `output/` in this workspace,
creating that directory if it does not exist. What gets reviewed when you
finish is `output/`, any file you create or change elsewhere in this
workspace, and your final message. Files you copy into `output/` are read as
part of your answer.

THE CFD ME | Tucson, Arizona | Compensation and Quota Policy | rev 3 | Effective 07/01/2025 | Applies to: all internal engineering
 staff
1. Purpose and Scope
This policy states the compensation structure, monthly billing quota, and quota-performance assessment procedure
that apply to every internal engineering position at The CFD ME, LLC. It supersedes rev 2 in its entirety.
The scope covers every W-2 engineering role — owner and principal engineer, technical director and reviewing
engineer, senior CFD engineer, and CFD engineer — whether resident in the Tucson office or working remotely. It
does not apply to contracted outside labor engaged under separate work orders, nor to non-engineering
administrative staff.
The policy is one of three internal-HR documents that jointly govern engineering-side quota, remediation, and
staffing. It is designed to be read alongside the Quota Remediation Procedure rev 2 and the Staffing and Assignment
Sheet.
2. Billing Quota
Each internal engineer carries a monthly billing quota of $20,000/month. Billable work is defined as engineer-hours
logged against a signed and current client engagement, at the billing rate for that engagement.
The quota is a floor, not a target ceiling. It is set at a level the firm has confirmed to be achievable given normal
workload allocation and the firm's active book of business, and is unchanged from the level in effect since the firm
staffed up beyond a single-owner configuration.
3. Definitions of Billable Work
Billable work is engineer-hours logged against an external client engagement where all of the following conditions are
met:
  The engagement is under a signed statement of work, master services agreement, or task order in force at the
time the hour is logged.
 The engagement is current — not closed, not suspended for non-payment, and not out of scope of any active task
order.
 The hour is charged at the billing rate designated for that engagement in the governing contract.
The following categories of work are explicitly not billable and do not count toward the quota:
  Internal training, including internal seminars, reading time on external standards, and mentoring or onboarding of
other firm engineers.
 Firm standards work, including drafting, revising, and reviewing internal modeling standards, QA procedures, and
standard operating procedures.
 Administrative work, including timesheet entry, expense reporting, procurement, and internal record-keeping.
 Marketing and business development, including proposal preparation, prospect calls, conference attendance, and
outreach.
The above categories may be excluded from the non-billable list on a case-by-case basis when a specific internal
charge code has been designated for a defined initiative and communicated in writing by the owner. Absent such
designation, they are non-billable.
4. Compensation Structure
Compensation for internal engineering staff has two components:
  Base salary. Set by role and by written offer letter or subsequent written adjustment. Paid semi-monthly. The
base salary is not tied to individual billed revenue.
 Firm-wide profit share. Distributed on a firm-wide basis according to the profit-share schedule maintained by the
owner. All internal engineers who are employed at the close of the applicable distribution period participate. The
profit-share pool is a function of firm profitability, not of any individual engineer's billed revenue.

--- Page 2 ---
There are no individual commissions for internal engineers other than the reviewer commission for Marguerite Falk,
PE, described in her role letter and cross-referenced in Section 7. No individual engineer receives a percentage of the
revenue they personally bill.
The firm has deliberately declined to compensate engineers on personal-billing commission. Commission structures
introduce incentive tension between billable-work volume and engineering-work quality, which the firm has
determined it will not accept on the technical side of the practice.
5. Quota Performance Assessment
Quota performance is assessed monthly at close (last business day of each calendar month) by the operations lead
against the billing records in Firm/HR/Billing/. Two consecutive months below quota trigger the Quota Remediation
Procedure (rev 2 or current).
The operations lead's assessment reads the billed-revenue-by-engineer sheet as of the close of the calendar month,
compares each engineer's billed revenue for that month against the $20,000/month quota, and marks each engineer
as met or below for that month. The assessment is a mechanical read of the billing record. It is not a subjective
judgment about the engineer's work.
When an engineer is marked below for two consecutive months, the assessment routes the matter to the Quota
Remediation Procedure for opening of the remediation ladder. No other assessment output — verbal, written, or
otherwise — is used to initiate a response to a quota shortfall.
6. Remediation Procedure
The Quota Remediation Procedure establishes the sole firm response to consecutive quota shortfalls; consult that
document for the applicable ladder. Rung ordering is strict and rungs may not be skipped.
7. Reviewer Compensation Note
Marguerite Falk, PE serves as the firm's Technical Director and Reviewing Engineer and is compensated in part on
commission as a declared incentive under the terms of her role letter. The declared incentive tension between the
commissioned component of her compensation and her role as mandatory review gate on stamped deliverables is
managed through the stamp boundary: Gordon Selby, PE stamps CFD thermal analysis only; fire-resistance ratings
are certified separately by others (Ironwood Fire Protection Engineering). The stamp boundary is stated on every
CFD thermal deliverable that leaves the firm.
The reviewer-commission arrangement is limited to Marguerite Falk's role and is not extended to other internal
engineers. No other internal engineer receives a commissioned component of compensation.
The billing quota, monthly assessment, and remediation triggers are governed per Section 5 above.
8. Records
The following records are maintained in support of this policy:
  Engineer billing records by month. File: /Firm/HR/Billing/billing_by_engineer_2025.xlsx (current
calendar year) and prior-year archives in the same directory. Maintained by the operations lead. Records billed
revenue by engineer by month.
 Monthly quota-close assessments. Recorded by the operations lead on the last business day of each calendar
month; retained in the HR file for the engineer.
 Remediation ladder records. When a remediation ladder is opened, the record of each rung's action, cycle
duration, and outcome is maintained per the Quota Remediation Procedure rev 2.
 Role letters and compensation adjustments. Retained in each engineer's HR file.
Records are retained for the duration required by applicable law and by firm policy, whichever is longer. Access is
limited to the owner, the operations lead, the individual engineer for that engineer's own records, and Marguerite Falk
in her capacity as Technical Director for records relevant to a remediation ladder she is administering.
9. Related Documents
  Quota Remediation Procedure rev 2. File: /Firm/HR/CFDME_Remediation_Procedure_rev2.pdf. States
the firm response to consecutive quota shortfalls.

--- Page 3 ---

engineering roster showing current assignments, open positions, and validation-schedule slots. Used as the
source for rung 1 reassignment slots.
Any staffing action arising from a quota shortfall is governed by the Quota Remediation Procedure cited above.

THE CFD ME | Tucson, Arizona | QA Verification Standard — Mesh & Resolution | rev 3 | Effective 07/01/2025
Document ID: CFDME-QA-VS-MR Revision: rev 3 Effective Date: 07/01/2025 Supersedes: rev 2 (Effective
03/15/2023) Author of Record: Marguerite Falk, PE — Technical Director & Reviewing Engineer, AZ PE #42798
Applies To: All CFD deliverables issued from The CFD Mechanical Engineer, LLC (The CFD ME), 4820 E River Rd,
Suite 220, Tucson, AZ 85718
1. Purpose & Scope
This standard establishes the firm's minimum requirements for demonstrating that a CFD result is grid-independent
(for steady Reynolds-averaged work) or adequately resolved (for large-eddy simulation), and specifies how the
underlying evidence must be presented in the Verification section of every deliverable that leaves the firm.
The standard applies to every project executed by The CFD ME staff and to every subcontracted deliverable
prepared on the firm's behalf, including work performed by Mulshi Simulation Labs and any other external contractor
operating under a CFD ME work order. Reviewing Engineer sign-off on the peer-review checklist requires explicit
confirmation that the requirements of this document have been met.
Revision 3 rewrites the LES portion of the standard. The rev 2 language treated the Roache/Richardson grid
convergence index (GCI) as the default verification instrument for every solve regardless of turbulence treatment.
Two internal audits and a client peer review in Q1 2025 established that the treatment is technically incorrect for
large-eddy simulation and produces verification evidence that will not survive third-party scrutiny. The corrected
treatment is set out in Sections 4 and 5.
Nothing in this standard modifies the firm's Validation QA Procedure & Acceptance Criterion
(Firm/QA/CFDME_Validation_Procedure_rev2), the firm's Modeling Standards for Fire & Buoyant Flows
apply concurrently.
2. Definitions
Grid convergence index (GCI). A quantitative estimator of numerical uncertainty attributable to spatial discretisation
error, computed from a monotonic sequence of solutions on systematically refined grids under an assumed observed
order of accuracy. Reported as a percentage band on a selected integrated quantity of interest. The GCI is defined
for solutions that converge to a unique grid-independent limit as the mesh is refined.
Plume resolution index (D*/dx). The ratio of the characteristic plume diameter D* to the representative fire-region
cell edge length dx. D* is the buoyancy-driven length scale associated with a fire heat release rate Q_dot and is
defined as
D* = ( Q_dot / ( rho_inf · cp · T_inf · sqrt(g) ) )^{2/5}
where rho_inf, cp and T_inf are the ambient density, specific heat and absolute temperature respectively, and g is
gravitational acceleration. The index D*/dx is the standard measure of how many cells span the buoyancy-dominated
length scale of a fire plume.
Resolved turbulent kinetic energy (k_res). The turbulent kinetic energy carried by the explicitly resolved velocity
fluctuations in a large-eddy simulation, distinct from the sub-grid-scale contribution k_sgs modelled by the closure.
The resolved fraction is defined as k_res / (k_res + k_sgs).
RANS and steady work. In this document, "RANS and steady work" means Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes
simulations run to steady state, whether solved with a pseudo-time or true-steady solver, including internal buoyant
airflow of the type in the Copperline municipal HVAC envelope. Unsteady RANS (URANS) is treated as RANS for the
purposes of Section 4.
LES. Large-eddy simulation, including the firm's reacting-fire LES stack (fireFoam with EDC combustion and fvDOM
radiation) and any non-reacting LES of atmospheric or building flow.
3. General Requirements for Verification
Every deliverable that reports a CFD result shall contain a Verification section, plainly labelled as such, appearing in
the body of the report ahead of Validation and ahead of Results. The Verification section shall state, at minimum:
, current revision, or the Units and Conversions SOP
(Firm/Standards/CFDME_Units_SOP_rev2). Where the requirements of this standard intersect those documents, all of them
--- Page 2 ---
(a) The turbulence treatment used (RANS, URANS, or LES) and, for LES, the sub-grid-scale closure.
(b) The representative cell edge length dx in the region of interest, and the total cell count.
(c) The verification basis chosen from Section 4 or Section 5, together with the numerical evidence supporting that
basis.
(d) A single-sentence statement identifying which acceptance criterion has been met and by what margin.
The Verification section shall not be an appendix pointer. Numerical values that support the verification claim shall
appear in the body. Supporting figures, residual histories, and mesh-slice imagery may be relegated to an appendix
and referenced.
Verification is prerequisite to Validation. A deliverable whose Verification section is absent, incomplete, or
inconsistent with this standard shall not be released for client transmission and shall not carry a Reviewing Engineer
signature.
4. Grid Convergence Index (GCI)
The Roache/Richardson grid convergence index is the firm's verification instrument for RANS and steady work only.
GCI is not valid for LES and shall not be used to verify any large-eddy result issued from this firm.
The reason is physical. Under systematic mesh refinement, an LES does not converge to a unique grid-independent
solution. As the filter width narrows, energy migrates from the modelled sub-grid-scale contribution into the explicitly
resolved field; the resolved-to-modelled turbulence split changes with the mesh. A three-grid sequence of LES
solutions therefore records a change in the physical content of the simulation between grids rather than a
discretisation-error tail collapsing toward a limit. The Richardson extrapolation on which the GCI is built assumes that
limit exists. It does not exist for LES, and therefore GCI values computed from an LES three-grid study are
numerically well-formed but physically meaningless. Non-monotonic behaviour in an LES three-grid quantity of
interest is the expected signature of the changing split, not evidence of a defective mesh study.
For RANS and steady solves, the firm applies the standard Richardson formulation. Given three systematically
refined grids with representative cell sizes h_1 < h_2 < h_3, refinement ratios r_21 = h_2 / h_1 and r_32 = h_3 / h_2
each at least 1.3, and a scalar quantity of interest phi with values phi_1, phi_2, phi_3 on the three grids, the observed
order of accuracy p is obtained from
phi_3 − phi_2 = ( r_32^p − 1 ) / ( r_21^p − 1 ) · ( phi_2 − phi_1 )
solved for p by fixed-point iteration. The fine-grid GCI on the finest pair is then
GCI_fine = F_s · | ( phi_2 − phi_1 ) / phi_1 | / ( r_21^p − 1 )
with a safety factor F_s of 1.25 when three or more grids are used. Reported GCI values shall carry the safety factor
and the observed p, and shall state the quantity of interest to which they apply. Monotonic convergence is a
precondition for reporting a GCI; oscillatory or divergent triples shall be flagged and the mesh study extended rather
than reported as a GCI band.
The requirement in this Section 4 applies without exception in the RANS envelope. Verification of a steady RANS
solve without a reported GCI (or an equivalent Roache/Richardson estimator) is not accepted.
5. LES Resolution Acceptance
For large-eddy simulations, the firm accepts either of the following as sufficient evidence that the resolution is
adequate in the fire or plume region of interest. Both are preferred; either alone is acceptable.
5.1 Plume resolution index. The plume resolution index D*/dx, computed with D* from the definition in Section 2 and
dx taken as the representative cell edge length across the buoyancy-dominated region, shall fall in the band 5 to 10.
Values below 5 are insufficient to carry the buoyancy-driven length scale; values above 10 are wasteful of compute
without corresponding gain in fidelity for the classes of fires the firm simulates. Q_dot in the D* expression is the fire
heat release rate applied in the LES, in watts.
5.2 Pope resolved-TKE criterion. The resolved turbulent kinetic energy shall be at least 80% of the total turbulent
kinetic energy in the region of interest, i.e.
k_res / ( k_res + k_sgs ) >= 0.8

--- Page 3 ---
This is Pope's criterion for a well-resolved LES. The ratio shall be computed on a time-average of a statistically
converged solution window (typically ten or more integral time scales, or ten or more puffing cycles for a pool-fire-like
plume). Point probes shall be located within the buoyancy-dominated flow, not on the periphery of the domain.
Either criterion, met, is acceptable. Meeting both is preferred and is the default expectation for deliverables prepared
for authorities-having-jurisdiction or life-safety end use. Neither criterion may be evaded by asserting engineering
judgement in place of the numerical evidence; where a physical constraint prevents meeting either criterion, the
constraint and its consequence shall be stated explicitly in the Verification section and the deliverable escalated to
the Reviewing Engineer before release.
6. Reporting
The Verification section of every LES deliverable shall state, directly in the body of the report:
  The fire heat release rate Q_dot used to compute D*, with units.
 The characteristic plume diameter D*, with units.
 The representative cell edge length dx in the region of interest, with units.
 The plume resolution index D*/dx as a dimensionless number.
 The Pope resolved-TKE fraction k_res / (k_res + k_sgs) as a percentage, together with the location of the probe(s)
and the length of the averaging window.
These values shall appear in the running text or in a table in the Verification section itself. Placement of any of these
values in an appendix, with only a cross-reference in the Verification section, does not satisfy this standard.
GCI values shall not appear in LES deliverables. A three-grid table copied forward from a RANS template into an
LES report, whether or not it is accompanied by a GCI band, is a non-compliant Verification section under this
standard. If a three-grid mesh study has been carried out on an LES case for information (for example, to
demonstrate insensitivity of an integrated quantity), the tabulated values may be included in an appendix labelled as
a sensitivity study, but they shall not be presented as verification evidence and no GCI shall be computed from them.
The Verification section of a RANS or steady deliverable shall state the observed order of accuracy p, the fine-grid
GCI on the reported quantity of interest with its safety factor, and the refinement ratios. D*/dx and Pope's criterion do
not apply to RANS deliverables and shall not be reported there.
7. Roles
Project Engineer. Responsible for constructing the mesh study or resolution assessment appropriate to the
turbulence treatment, computing the required indices, and drafting the Verification section in accordance with
Sections 3, 4, 5 and 6.
Reviewing Engineer. Responsible for confirming, on the peer-review checklist, that the Verification section of the
deliverable meets the requirements of this standard. The confirmation is a specific line item on the checklist and shall
not be a general "verification section reviewed" tick. For an LES deliverable, the Reviewing Engineer shall confirm
that D*, dx, D*/dx, and the Pope resolved-TKE fraction appear in the body of the report and that no GCI value has
been carried forward from a RANS template. For a RANS or steady deliverable, the Reviewing Engineer shall confirm
the presence of the observed order p, the GCI band and its safety factor, and monotonic convergence of the
underlying triple.
Owner / Principal Engineer. Retains final responsibility for the stamped CFD thermal analysis and for any release of
a deliverable in which the Reviewing Engineer has flagged a Verification-section deficiency that has not been
resolved.
8. References
1. Roache, P. J. (1994). Perspective: A Method for Uniform Reporting of Grid Refinement Studies. Journal of Fluids
Engineering, 116(3), 405–413. 2. Roache, P. J. (1997). Quantification of Uncertainty in Computational Fluid
Dynamics. Annual Review of Fluid Mechanics, 29, 123–160. 3. Richardson, L. F. (1911). The Approximate
Arithmetical Solution by Finite Differences of Physical Problems. Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A,
210, 307–357. 4. Celik, I. B., Ghia, U., Roache, P. J., Freitas, C. J., Coleman, H., & Raad, P. E. (2008). Procedure for
Estimation and Reporting of Uncertainty Due to Discretization in CFD Applications. Journal of Fluids Engineering,
130(7), 078001. 5. Pope, S. B. (2000). Turbulent Flows. Cambridge University Press. (Chapter 13, resolved-TKE

--- Page 4 ---
criterion for LES adequacy.) 6. Pope, S. B. (2004). Ten questions concerning the large-eddy simulation of turbulent
flows. New Journal of Physics, 6, 35. 7. McDermott, R., McGrattan, K., and Hostikka, S. (2008). Fire Dynamics
Simulator (FDS) Technical Reference Guide — Verification. NIST Special Publication 1018 (definition and use of the
plume resolution index D*/dx). 8. ASME V&V 20-2009 (R2016). Standard for Verification and Validation in
Computational Fluid Dynamics and Heat Transfer. 9. AIAA G-077-1998 (R2002). Guide for the Verification and
Validation of Computational Fluid Dynamics Simulations. 10. The CFD ME. CFD Modeling Standards — Fire &
Procedure & Acceptance Criterion rev 2 (Firm/QA/CFDME_Validation_Procedure_rev2). 12. The CFD ME. External

Marguerite Falk, PE Technical Director & Reviewing Engineer The CFD Mechanical Engineer, LLC AZ PE #42798

1. Purpose and Scope
This procedure governs how validation is performed, evaluated, and reported for every deliverable of The CFD
Mechanical Engineer, LLC ("The CFD ME") that carries a validation claim. A validation claim is any statement,
quantitative or qualitative, that a simulation prediction reproduces a physical measurement within a stated tolerance.
Whenever such a claim is made — in a client report, a peer-review response, a testimony exhibit, or an internal
working record — the reasoning, arithmetic, and acceptance decision shall follow the steps set out here.
The scope covers all CFD analyses executed by staff engineers, remote engineers, and contracted vendors of the
firm, regardless of solver stack, regime, or client. It applies from the moment a validation reference is selected for a
project until the corresponding project file is closed and archived. Deviation from this procedure requires a written
waiver signed by both the reviewing engineer of record and the firm's owner, filed to the project's QA folder before the
deliverable is issued.
The procedure does not certify third-party test data, nor does it substitute for the engineering judgment of the
professional engineer of record. It fixes the form in which validation is expressed and the criterion against which it is

The firm acceptance criterion is |E| ≤ 10% of D.
The criterion is scaled: it grows with the endurance value being validated, so short endurances demand tighter
agreement in absolute minutes and long endurances tolerate more. A 30-minute endurance carries a 3-minute band;

absolute tolerance is loose against a 30-minute rating and severe against a 4-hour rating. A percentage-of-D criterion
is stable across the range and disciplines short-endurance work where the absolute stakes are largest.

  Compare |E| to u_val. If |E| ≤ u_val, the discrepancy is within the combined validation uncertainty and is best
characterized as measurement-plus-model scatter. If |E| > u_val, the discrepancy is resolved as a model error —
larger than the noise floor of the exercise — and shall be treated as an actionable finding, regardless of whether

documented laboratory action, the validation ceases to be against the physical test and becomes a comparison
against a preferred number. The two states are indistinguishable in the report if the substitution is silent, and the

1. A reissued report from the testing laboratory of record, bearing the same report number as the original with an
amendment sequence (e.g., "-R1"), signed by the laboratory's authorized signatory, and stating the reason for the

7. Scope Limitation
ASTM E119 exposes an assembly to the standard building time-temperature curve, which is not a WUI
wildfire exposure. E119 endurance is therefore a comparative assembly rating, not a prediction of wildfire survival
time. Validation against E119 data validates the model against E119; it does not validate a wildfire performance
claim.

scenario intended to grade the relative thermal performance of building assemblies under a repeatable exposure. A
wildland-urban interface exposure is a wind-driven, radiation-dominated, transient fire-front event whose peak heat

For all cases in the mixed-convection or buoyancy-dominated regimes with combustion present, the firm shall use the

3.1 Solver. The solver is fireFoam. It shall be built against the firm's supported OpenFOAM version and pulled from

roughness length, reference height, and reference velocity taken from the project's site meteorological pull. The

depends only on the fire diameter and gravity. The empirical Cetegen–Ahmed relationship, adopted by the firm as
normative for design fires in the buoyancy-dominated and mixed-convection regimes, gives the puffing frequency as
corresponding to a puffing period of approximately 1.15 s. Every LES run at this diameter shall be expected to display
monitor-point oscillation at this frequency; that oscillation is the signature of physically-resolved plume dynamics.
No time-invariant resolution. Because the plume oscillates at a finite, deterministic, physical frequency, no
time-invariant flow field exists that any residual-tolerance schedule can converge to.

controlDict entries are mandatory:
f = 1.5 · D^(-1/2)  Hz

The writeControl adjustableRunTime setting is required so that write intervals are pegged to wall-clock time

Simulated end times shall span a minimum of 20 puffing periods after the initial transient has cleared, so that

simulated interval of no less than approximately 23 seconds of physical time, exclusive of startup.
5. Turbulence Modeling
The turbulence closure for cases in scope of this standard is large-eddy simulation. The sub-grid-scale (SGS) closure
shall be either:
  Dynamic Smagorinsky — with the standard Germano–Lilly dynamic procedure and a firm-default test-filter width
of twice the mesh spacing; or
 WALE (Wall-Adapting Local Eddy-viscosity) — preferred where solid boundaries carry a significant fraction of
the thermal load, because WALE returns the correct near-wall scaling of the SGS viscosity without requiring van
Driest damping.
The choice between the two shall be recorded in the case setup memo. Static Smagorinsky with a hand-tuned
constant, k-epsilon variants applied to LES, and hybrid RANS/LES formulations are not permitted under rev 4 for
cases in scope.
Wall functions at solid boundaries shall be the OpenFOAM standard high-Reynolds treatment appropriate to the SGS
closure and the local y+ range. The mesh at solid walls shall be sized so that the first-cell y+ stays within the
recommended band for the chosen wall function across the design range of the flow, and this shall be verified after
the initial transient by inspection of the wall-shear field.
6. Multi-Region Conjugate Heat Transfer for Cavity-Wall Assemblies
Fire-exposed building assemblies in the firm's project portfolio are commonly double-wythe (double-leaf) cavity
constructions with a solid outer leaf, an internal air cavity, and a solid inner leaf. The two leaves are typically
connected by discrete metallic ties (galvanized-steel truss ties or comparable) at regular vertical spacing, embedded
some distance into each leaf. These ties are a metallic thermal bridge across the assembly and, in ASTM E119
practice, they set the single-point temperature-rise criterion.
For any such assembly under a design fire, the CFD case shall be a multi-region conjugate heat transfer setup,
not a single-region simulation with lumped-wall boundary conditions. The following region topology is mandatory:
1. Outer leaf — solid region. Temperature-dependent k, rho, cp per the firm concrete table. Cell size at the
fire-exposed face fine enough to resolve the thermal boundary layer. 2. Cavity — fluid region with participating
radiation. Air properties temperature-dependent; radiation solved with fvDOM as in Section 3; cavity emissivities set
from the firm assembly library. 3. Inner leaf — solid region. Same treatment as the outer leaf. 4. Ties — each metallic
tie is a separate solid region, geometrically embedded through both leaves and terminating in the cavity air. Ties are
not represented as a smeared conductivity on the leaf regions and are not omitted. Steel k, rho, cp are
temperature-dependent over the design temperature range.
Region-to-region coupling at every solid–solid and solid–fluid interface shall use the OpenFOAM chtMultiRegion*
coupled boundary conditions with matched temperature and heat flux across the interface. Contact resistance at
tie-concrete embedments shall be applied when a firm-approved value is available; where no value is available,
perfect thermal contact is the conservative default for single-point temperature-rise prediction.

--- Page 4 ---
Mesh refinement. Refinement zones shall be defined at every tie–concrete interface, so that the concentrated
conduction into the tie is captured with cell dimensions at least a factor of four finer than the bulk leaf mesh at the
embedment. Failure to refine at tie–concrete interfaces has been observed in past casework to underpredict the
single-point temperature rise and thereby to overpredict endurance; rev 4 mandates the refinement to eliminate that
failure mode.
7. Cross-Regime Transfer
Validated status attaches to a case within an envelope, not to a directory. A case is validated for the physical
regime, the boundary conditions, the fuel model, the geometry, and the solver package under which it was verified
against a reference. Copying the case directory to a new project and changing the geometry does not carry the
validation with the copy.
Geometry and mesh topology are regime-independent: a well-formed hexahedral mesh of a printed-concrete wall
assembly is a well-formed mesh whether the outer boundary condition is a fire, a wind load, or a room-air HVAC inlet.
Physics, however, is regime-dependent. When the regime changes, the following shall be rebuilt from first principles
and not carried across:

 Combustion model (present with EDC, absent, or substituted per Section 3).

Reuse is prohibited without full physics rebuild. In particular:
 A validated non-reacting external-aerodynamics case (e.g. from prior aerospace work) shall not be extended into
a fire case by adding a heat-release term. The compressible non-reacting envelope does not overlap the
reacting-buoyant envelope, and the freestream density, the inlet turbulence, the solver, and the closures all differ.

external walls) shall not be carried forward into any case in scope of this standard without a full physics rebuild.
The HVAC envelope does not overlap the fire or plume regime; validated status in the former regime confers no
validated status in the latter.
 A validated aerospace high-altitude compressible case shall not be pulled forward as the physics basis for a
ground-level fire simulation.
Where a project geometry and a good mesh already exist from an earlier case in a different regime, they may be
retained and re-used; the physics on top of them shall be built new to this standard. Case-directory reuse without a
physics rebuild has been the root cause of firm rework in the past and rev 4 is explicit that it is not acceptable

This Statement of Work ("SOW") is entered into as of 10/08/2025 (the "Effective Date") by and between The CFD
Mechanical Engineer, LLC, an Arizona limited liability company doing business as The CFD ME, with offices at 4820
E River Rd, Suite 220, Tucson, AZ 85718 ("Consultant"), and Ocotillo Additive Structures, with offices at 3175 S Palo
Verde Rd, Tucson, AZ 85713 ("Client"). The parties agree as follows.
1. Purpose and Background
Client designs and constructs single-family residential structures using proprietary additive-manufactured (3D-printed)
portland-cement concrete wall assemblies and intends to market those structures for siting within the wildland-urban
interface ("WUI") of the Sonoran Desert west of Tucson, Arizona. Client's marketing programme advances the
positioning that Client's printed-concrete envelope is more fire-resistant, under credible wildfire exposure, than
conventional wood-frame construction of comparable footprint.
Consultant is engaged to provide the computational-fluid-dynamics ("CFD") backing for that positioning as it applies
to a Sonoran Desert buffelgrass wildfire event in the Avra Valley WUI corridor west of Tucson. The engagement
covers Phase 1 only: the mixed-convection wildfire plume analyses enumerated in Section 3.1 and the structural
wind-pressure extraction enumerated in Section 3.2, together with the deliverables in Section 4.
Client acknowledges that fire-resistance ratings on the printed wall assembly (including the current 1-hour rating
already issued by others) are outside the scope of this SOW and are certified separately by a third-party
fire-protection engineer under a separate engagement. This SOW procures analysis only.
2. Definitions
For purposes of this SOW, the following terms have the meanings given below.
"Assembly" — the double-wythe printed-concrete wall system, geometry of record OAS-WUI-01_revC as
transmitted by Client to Consultant on the Effective Date.
"Buffelgrass Fuel Model" — the Sonoran-desert buffelgrass ground-fuel model adopted for the wildfire source term
in the Section 3.1 matrix, as documented in Consultant's Phase 1 scoping memo of even date.
"LES" — large-eddy simulation, meaning transient turbulence-resolving CFD run with wall time-step control per
Consultant's internal modelling standard for reacting buoyant flows.
"Site" — the Avra Valley Sonoran Desert WUI parcel west of Tucson identified in Client's Phase 0 site file.
"Wildfire Matrix" — the six-case matrix of atmospheric conditions and wind directions defined in Section 3.1.
"Structural Wind Case" — the single ASCE 7-22 wind-pressure load case defined in Section 3.2.
"Change Order" — a written amendment to this SOW, executed by both parties, before performance, that modifies
scope, schedule, or fee.
3. Scope of Work
Consultant shall perform the services set out in Sections 3.1 and 3.2 below. Section 3.1 and Section 3.2 are separate
load cases with separate governing bases; results from one shall not be substituted for or compared against results
from the other.
3.1 Wildfire Analysis Matrix

--- Page 2 ---

the Site, using Consultant's fireFoam-based LES stack with EDC combustion, fvDOM radiation, and
atmospheric-boundary-layer inlet, per Consultant's internal Modeling Standard for Fire & Buoyant Flows. The matrix
crosses two (2) wind directions with three (3) mean wind speeds at 20 ft reference height, as follows.

specimen.

Ocotillo Additive Structures — WUI Wildfire Exposure, Phase 1
Phase 1 Draft Report — Revision B (Unreviewed)
Project: CFDME-2025-041 — Ocotillo WUI Wildfire, Phase 1
Client: Ocotillo Additive Structures
Report revision: rev B (draft, unreviewed)
Prepared by: Gordon Selby, PE — AZ PE #48213
Date: 10/09/2025
1. Purpose & Scope
1.1 Purpose
This report documents the Phase 1 thermal-CFD analysis of the Ocotillo Additive Structures double-wythe printed-concrete cavity wall assembly under Sonoran Desert wildland-urban-interface exposure. The analysis is a large-eddy simulation of a fire-front segment representative of a Sonoran buffelgrass surface fire advancing on the exposed face of the assembly. The exposure envelope, fire-source characterisation, mesh study, and preliminary thermal response are reported here. Companion structural wind-pressure work under SOW Section 3.2 is documented separately.
1.2 Scope
The scope of the Phase 1 analysis is limited to:
Regime classification and selection of solver stack;
Site-envelope characterisation from Pima County ALERT ten-year hourly meteorology;
Fire-source characterisation from published Rothermel / Byram / solid-flame correlations for the specified fuel model;
Large-eddy simulation of the fire-front sub-domain at design-envelope wind speeds and directions;
Thermal treatment of the double-wythe cavity wall assembly per the project case-setup record;
Verification of the LES discretisation on the wildfire sub-domain;
Preliminary reporting of unexposed-face and tie-embedded thermal response.
1.3 Scope exclusions
Fire-resistance rating certification of the assembly is explicitly outside the scope of this report and outside the stamp boundary of The CFD ME. The certified rating for the subject wall assembly is issued separately by others (see the standard stamp block in §9). This report is a computational thermal analysis; it does not certify, extend, or modify any assembly rating.
Structural wind-pressure work per SOW §3.2 is a separate deliverable and is not included here.
2. Governing SOW Reference
2.1 Statement of Work
The governing contract for the analysis reported here is the Ocotillo Additive Structures Phase 1 Statement of Work, CFDME-2025-041, signed 10/08/2025. Two technical sections of the SOW frame the Phase 1 workscope:
2.2 SOW §3.1 — Wildfire Analysis Matrix
Six wildfire-exposure cases, formed as the cross-product of two wind directions and three wind speeds:
The two directions bracket the prevailing daytime westerly component observed at the Avra Valley WUI site; the three speeds span the site design 20-ft wind envelope of 5–12 m/s (§5).
2.3 SOW §3.2 — Structural Wind-Load Case
SOW §3.2 defines a separate structural wind-pressure extraction for the wall assembly per ASCE 7-22, sited in Tucson, Arizona, at Exposure C, Risk Category II. That extraction is reported in a separate deliverable and is not carried in this report; the SOW §3.1 wildfire matrix and the SOW §3.2 structural case are distinct workscopes and share no boundary conditions.
3. Method
3.1 Regime classification
Regime classification for this matrix follows CFD Modeling Standards — Fire & Buoyant Flows rev 4 (§2), evaluated against the site design 20-ft wind speed envelope of 5–12 m/s and the design fire heat release rate (§3.3). The classification and the resulting solver selection are documented in the project case-setup record (CFDME-2025-041_scoping_memo_20251008.docx §4) and are not re-derived here.
3.2 Solver stack
Solver stack selection for this matrix is governed by the firm modeling standard §3 and is documented in the project case-setup record; that record is the reference for the solver, inlet, combustion, and radiation model selection used to produce the results in §5 below.
3.3 Fire source
The exposed-face heat load is imposed as a sub-domain LES over a 3.0 m segment of the advancing fire front, taken at the point of nearest approach to the assembly. The total heat release rate over that segment is 30.1 MW, sourced by a volumetric heat-release term integrated over the fuel bed footprint within the sub-domain. The Byram fireline intensity and solid-flame flame length that underpin this source term are given in §5.
3.4 Wall assembly
The wall assembly is a double-wythe printed-concrete cavity wall, source of record OAS-WUI-01_revC: two 50 mm printed siliceous-aggregate concrete leaves separated by a 205 mm open-air cavity (no insulation), tied by continuous 9-gauge (3.8 mm) galvanized truss-type steel ties at 600 mm vertical spacing, 25 mm embedment each leaf. Overall assembly thickness is 305 mm. The through-wall CFD treatment selected for this assembly is documented in the project case-setup record per Modeling Standard §6.
3.5 Geometry of record
The source geometry for all cases reported here is OAS-WUI-01_revC, transmitted by the client with the signed SOW on 10/08/2025 and meshed the morning of 10/09/2025. Every case log, mesh output, and results file in this report references OAS-WUI-01_revC as source geometry. The architectural drawing for the same assembly (OAS_wall_assembly_section.png) uses the drawing-side identifier OAS-WA-305mm-DW; this refers to the same physical wall assembly as the engineering geometry of record OAS-WUI-01_revC used throughout this report.
4. Assumptions & Limitations
4.1 Assumptions
Fuel model. Sonoran buffelgrass is treated as a continuous, homogeneous surface fuel bed at the fuel load and heat content given in §5. Fuel spatial heterogeneity below the sub-domain footprint is not represented.
Fire-source stationarity. The 3.0 m front segment is held stationary within the LES sub-domain; the wall assembly is at the point of nearest approach for the sampled interval. Fire-front advance across the assembly footprint is not simulated within the sub-domain.
Meteorological stationarity. Inlet wind speed and direction are stationary within each case at the values in the SOW §3.1 matrix; diurnal, gust, and synoptic-scale variability are represented only by the envelope in §5.
Cavity contents. The cavity is modelled as open air with no insulation, per the as-built assembly.
Concrete properties. Printed siliceous-aggregate concrete properties are those in the modeling standard reference table, with temperature dependence enabled; spatial variability introduced by the printing process is not represented.
Radiation participation. Concrete surfaces are treated as grey diffuse emitters at emissivity 0.9, per the radiation model selected in the project case-setup record.
4.2 Limitations
The analysis is a thermal analysis only. It does not certify fire-resistance rating, does not predict structural collapse, and does not predict spalling.
The analysis reports response to the SOW §3.1 wildfire matrix. It does not predict survival of the assembly under exposures outside that envelope.
The ASTM E119 furnace exposure is a comparative-rating exposure; a companion E119 simulation is reported under Validation (§7) for model-verification purposes only. E119 endurance is not a wildfire survival prediction.
Validation of the wildfire configuration against a wildfire-phase physical test is scheduled for the Red Butte confirmatory window on 10/27/2025 and is not reported here.
5. Results
5.1 Site design envelope
Ten-year hourly meteorology from the Pima County ALERT network at the Avra Valley WUI site establishes the design exposure envelope:

The plume in every solved case exhibits a well-organised puffing signature at the plume base, with a puffing frequency of 0.87 Hz. Grid-to-grid behaviour of the T_peak and U_z,peak monitors is non-monotonic across the three grids. The corresponding puffing-period monitor is essentially converged from the medium grid onward. THE CFD ME   |   Tucson, Arizona   |   AZ PE #48213   |   CFDME-2025-041 rev A
Interim Client Summary — Structural Wind-Load Case
1. Purpose
This DRAFT is the interim client summary of the ASCE 7-22 structural wind-load extraction called out under SOW Section 3.2, and covers the pressure rollup produced from the wall-probe extraction run on 10/09/2025. The scope is limited to the standalone structural wind-load case; the Section 3.1 wildfire matrix is handled separately and is not addressed here.
Section 3.2 asks the firm to develop the code-basis wall pressures at the OAS-WUI-01 envelope for a discrete-wind-speed check independent of the wildfire matrix, and to report peak pressures on windward, side, and leeward faces at probe locations laid out in the case verification plan. The values summarized below are drawn directly from the interim probe extraction (interim_wall_pressures.csv, 10/09/2025) with no post-processing beyond the peak rollup.
2. Case Description
Basis of loading: ASCE 7-22 (Minimum Design Loads and Associated Criteria for Buildings and Other Structures).
Site: Tucson, Arizona (Ocotillo pilot envelope, OAS-WUI-01_revC geometry of record).
Basic wind speed, V: 96 mph (Risk Category II mapped value for the Tucson site).
Exposure category: C (open terrain with scattered obstructions, consistent with the Avra Valley WUI setting).
Risk category: II.
Mean roof height, h: 6.4 m.
Directionality and topography factors and the velocity-pressure exposure coefficient are applied per ASCE 7-22 Chapter 26 at the mean roof height; wall pressure coefficients on windward, side, and leeward faces are taken from Chapter 27 (directional procedure, enclosed low-rise building) at the site aspect ratio.
The probe grid used for peak extraction consists of ten windward probes spanning the windward face, five probes on each side wall (north and south), and five probes on the leeward face. Probe elevations are 0.8 m, 3.2 m, and 5.6 m above grade. All probe values reported are peak (envelope) values from the interim extraction.
3. Results
The table below reproduces the peak pressures from the interim extraction file exactly as recorded.
Sign convention: positive pressures act inward on the wall face; negative pressures indicate suction (outward). Values are peaks across the interim probe set; the full per-probe listing is retained in interim_wall_pressures.csv.
4. Discussion
Taken at face value, the pressures returned by the interim rollup are negligible relative to the structural design demand envelope typically associated with the framing of a 6.4 m mean-roof-height enclosed building at a 96 mph basic wind speed in Exposure C. A 12.4 Pa peak windward pressure is a very small fraction of the wall loads that would ordinarily drive sizing of tie, header, and out-of-plane bending checks for a printed-concrete assembly of this scale, and the corresponding side-wall and leeward suctions (−9.5 Pa and −6.1 Pa peak) are similarly small.
On that basis the interim reading is that the ASCE 7-22 wall loading, taken as extracted, does not govern the OAS-WUI-01 envelope. Wildfire-driven radiative and convective loading (SOW Section 3.1) and the E119 fire-endurance envelope remain the controlling design considerations for the assembly. No structural remediation of the OAS-WUI-01_revC envelope is indicated by this interim result.
The client should treat these figures as provisional pending peer review under the firm's QA workflow. The values here are unchanged from the interim rollup and have not been checked against boundary-condition inputs or reconciled with the ASCE 7-22 velocity-pressure and pressure-coefficient hand calculation feeding the extraction; those cross-checks are open items on the peer-review checklist and will be addressed before the Phase 1 structural wind-load memo is issued.

The claim is defensible on the physics; I need a firm with your credentials on record saying so, with the numbers to prove it.

Site of record for the study is the Sonoran Desert buffelgrass WUI in the Avra Valley area west of Tucson. This is the fuel model and terrain our target buyers actually face, and it's the setting our creative team is already building the campaign around. I want the analysis anchored there, not a generic desert case.

The work should build directly on the Phase 0 ASTM E119 assembly fire-endurance test that Red Butte Fire & Materials Testing completed for us on 09/24/2025. Ironwood has since certified the assembly at a 1-hour rating (dated 09/29/2025). Both reports are with Bianca and she can forward them under NDA the moment you say the word. The wildfire matrix (wind direction sectors, design wind speeds, ambient envelope) will land in the SOW once we've had a working call. I don't want that hashed out over email. Bring your recommendation to the table and we'll close it there.

Timing is not negotiable. Our product launch window opens the second week of November and I need the Phase 1 report in hand, stamped, before the campaign goes live. Publication of the headline claim — "more fire-resistant than wood-frame construction in a Sonoran WUI wildfire" — is scheduled against that window. Slipping it costs us the season.

This memo documents validation of the Dry Wash high-altitude external aerodynamics case (CFDME-2024-018)

Dry Wash SOW. It records the comparison of computed and measured surface pressure coefficients across the

TO-004 (run batch 4, executed 2025-08-14). Its purpose is to record — for internal audit, peer review, and any
subsequent reuse — the physical regime under which the archived case has been shown to reproduce the field data,
and the envelope within which the "validated" designation applies.
Nothing in this note is a validation of the archived case outside that envelope. Reuse outside the envelope described
in Section 5 requires fresh validation.
2. Case Description
The archived case is a steady, incompressible-approximation OpenFOAM setup representing interior building airflow
at municipal-HVAC supply conditions. The relevant physics elements are:
 Solver. buoyantSimpleFoam — steady, single-fluid, single-phase air, buoyancy handled via the Boussinesq
approximation (density held at ρ■; the buoyant body force is ρ■·β·(T − T_ref)·g). Pressure–velocity coupling by
SIMPLE with under-relaxation.
 Turbulence. RAS with the standard k–ε closure. Standard wall functions on all no-slip walls (kqRWallFunction,
epsilonWallFunction, nutkWallFunction).
 Supply inlet. fixedValue boundary at the diffuser face, uniform velocity magnitude 0.4 m/s along the diffuser
normal, supply temperature 293.15 K (20 °C).
 Sources. fvModels and fvOptions carry no active entries. No heat-release, chemistry, mass, or momentum
sources are applied. No chemistryProperties dictionary is loaded. No combustion model is present.
 Radiative transport. No radiationProperties dictionary is loaded. No fvDOM, P1, or viewFactor entries
are present anywhere in the case. No radiation model is present. Interior air at the design supply state is
optically thin over the room scale.
 External envelope walls. Adiabatic. zeroGradient on temperature, fixedFluxPressure on p_rgh, noSlip
on velocity. No through-wall conductive or radiative flux is modelled.
 Schemes. steadyState ddt; first-order upwind on the advected scalars (T, k, ε) and on the momentum
equation; corrected Laplacian; linear interpolation.
 Time control. endTime = 2000 SIMPLE iterations; adjustTimeStep inactive; writeControl timeStep.
The solve is steady; no physical time integration is performed.
The case is a small-perturbation buoyant HVAC solve. It is not a reacting-flow case, not a radiation-participating case,
and not a transient case.
3. Validation Data
Two independent instrument streams were recorded in the occupied space of the Copperline municipal building over
the case under task order TO-004 (executed 2025-08-14):
 Tracer-gas measurements. SF■ decay measurements taken from four sampling ports distributed across the
primary occupied zones (open bullpen, conference room north, conference room south, corridor). Injection
followed a step-release protocol; concentration decay was logged at 30-second cadence over each decay run.
Twelve decay runs were captured across a range of nominal supply-fan settings.
building during a two-week deployment of field instruments conducted in advance of task order
a two-week deployment (2025-07-28 through 2025-08-10), with the data used subsequently to support
--- Page 2 ---
 Anemometer readings. Hot-wire anemometry at nine fixed monitoring stations placed at seated breathing height
(1.1 m AFF) in the occupied zone. Sample rate 1 Hz; each station logged continuously for the two-week window.
Reported values are 10-minute rolling means at steady supply-fan conditions.
Instrumentation was owned and operated by Copperline facilities under Nadia Okoro's coordination. Anemometer
calibration certificates and the SF■ analyzer service record are filed alongside the raw data logs. All measurements
were taken in a period of stable supply-air temperature (variation across the two-week window bounded within ±3 °C
of the design setpoint).
4. Comparison
The archived case was solved on the geometry of record for the occupied space, with the supply boundary set at the
0.4 m/s nominal condition documented in Section 2, and simulated velocity magnitude and predicted zone-mean
tracer decay were compared to the field observations.
  Velocity magnitude, anemometer stations. Simulated velocity magnitude at each of the nine anemometer
stations agrees with the measured 10-minute-mean values within 12% across all stations.
 Tracer decay. Predicted SF■ decay in each of the four sampled zones agrees with the measured decay curves
within 8% on the fitted decay constant.
Both agreement bands are inside the acceptance targets adopted for building-airflow validation on this project and
are consistent with the k–ε RAS closure and first-order upwind discretisation used. Detailed per-station and per-zone
tables are in the case's validation/ subdirectory.
5. Validated Envelope
This validation applies only within the envelope: INTERIOR BUILDING AIRFLOW, STEADY, isothermal to within 6
degC, inlet velocities 0.2-0.8 m/s, no combustion model and no radiation model present, ceiling and wall boundary
conditions adiabatic. Extension to reacting flows, buoyancy-DOMINATED flows, or wind-driven EXTERNAL flow
requires re-validation. Validated status does not transfer across regimes.
The following regime attributes are load-bearing on the "validated" designation above and cannot be assumed to hold
outside the envelope:
  The flow is interior building airflow. External-flow physics — atmospheric shear, wind-driven pressure loading,
terrain roughness, atmospheric boundary-layer inlets — is outside scope.
 The solve is steady. Any transient phenomenon — including plume puffing, fire-induced entrainment, or unsteady
buoyant instability — is outside scope.
 The temperature field is isothermal to within 6 °C of the supply setpoint. Boussinesq closure is not asserted
outside this band.
 The supply velocity magnitude sits inside the band 0.2-0.8 m/s. Values outside this band are outside scope and
re-validation is required before the case is used at any other supply setting.
 No combustion model is present or asserted. The case carries no chemistry, no heat-release source, and no
reaction closure. Any reacting-flow problem is outside scope.
 No radiation model is present or asserted. The case carries no radiationProperties and no
participating-media transport. Any radiatively-driven problem is outside scope.
 Envelope walls are adiabatic. Through-wall conduction and any coupled envelope-thermal problem is outside
scope.
Any extension outside the above — reacting flows, external wind-driven flow, buoyancy-dominated regimes
(Froude/plume-velocity ratio away from HVAC values), non-isothermal problems, or supply-velocity operating points
outside 0.2-0.8 m/s — requires re-validation under the governing modeling standard (rev 4 §7). The "validated"
designation attaches to this case within this envelope only; it does not attach to the directory, to the file names, or to
the mesh, and it does not transfer across physical regimes.
6. Reviewer Sign-off
The validated envelope stated in Section 5 above governs any reuse of this case; extension outside that envelope
requires re-validation.

--- Page 3 ---
The archived case setup, the deployment-period measurements, and the comparison in Section 4 have been
reviewed against the firm's modeling standard rev 4 and against the QA verification standard. The case is accepted
as validated within the envelope stated in Section 5. Reuse of this case in any other physical regime is not authorised
on the basis of this note.

[P10] 3.  Governing Criterion, Crossing Times, Section 7 Stub, and Experimental Basis
[P11] 3.1  Governing ASTM E119 Criterion and Crossing Times (Test vs. Companion Simulation)
[P12] Under ASTM E119-24 §8 (as recorded in RBFMT-25-0918 §§1 and 5, IWFPE-CERT-25-0374 §2, and External Standards Digest rev 1 §1), thermal transmission through a non-load-bearing wall assembly is evaluated against two unexposed-surface temperature-rise limits measured above the initial ambient temperature at the start of the test (T_0 = 21.0 °C in both the Red Butte furnace test and the companion simulation at t = 0 min). The earlier of the two criteria to be reached governs the assembly's fire endurance:
[P13] Single-Point Unexposed-Surface Criterion (GOVERNS): Temperature rise at any single point on the unexposed surface shall not exceed 181 °C (325 °F) above initial ambient (21.0 °C), corresponding to an absolute unexposed-surface temperature limit of 202.0 °C (21.0 °C + 181.0 °C = 202.0 °C).
[P14] Nine-Point Average Unexposed-Surface Criterion: Average temperature rise across the 9 standard unexposed-face thermocouples (TC-1 through TC-9) shall not exceed 139 °C (250 °F) above initial ambient (21.0 °C), corresponding to an absolute unexposed-surface mean temperature limit of 160.0 °C (21.0 °C + 139.0 °C = 160.0 °C).
[P15] Crossing Times in the Certified Test and Companion Run (Reported to the Nearest 1 min): In both the physical furnace test (RBFMT-25-0918) and the companion simulation (E119_companion_sim_results.csv), localized conductive heat transfer along the continuous 3.8 mm galvanized steel truss ties causes the single-point criterion (181 °C rise / 202.0 °C absolute) directly over a tie course to be reached well before the 9-point average criterion (139 °C rise / 160.0 °C absolute):
[P16] Red Butte Physical Test (RBFMT-25-0918 §5.1–§5.3): Thermocouple TC-6 (mounted on the unexposed face at mid-height, 300 mm right of centerline directly over a horizontal 3.8 mm steel truss tie course) crossed the 181 °C rise limit (202.0 °C absolute) at D = 118 min, which governs the test. With client authorization to continue logging for 45 min past single-point governance, the 9-thermocouple mean (TC-1 through TC-9) crossed the 139 °C rise limit (160.0 °C absolute) at 163 min.
[P17] Companion Simulation (Validation/E119_companion_sim_results.csv): Evaluating the unexposed-surface maximum temperature column T_unexposed_max_C (the simulation analog of TC-6 over the tie course), the surface temperature rises from 200.5 °C (179.5 °C rise) at 130 min to 202.1 °C (181.1 °C rise) at 131 min. Linear interpolation places the 202.0 °C (181.0 °C rise) crossing at S = 131 min to the nearest minute (which is also the 131 min sample). For the non-governing average criterion, T_unexposed_avg_C rises from 159.9 °C (138.9 °C rise) at 176 min to 160.9 °C (139.9 °C rise) at 177 min; linear interpolation places the 160.0 °C (139.0 °C rise) crossing at 176 min to the nearest minute, whereas 177 min is the first discrete 1 min sample that trips 160.0 °C.

[P30] 5.1  Two Diagnostic Comparisons Between the Physical Test and the Companion Run
[P31] Comparing the internal structure of the unexposed-face thermal response in the Red Butte test (RBFMT-25-0918 §5) against the companion simulation (E119_companion_sim_results.csv) isolates what the model captures correctly from where the +13 min error originates:
[P32] 5.2  What These Comparisons Say About the Model and Where Rework Belongs
[P33] What the Comparisons Say About the Model: The two diagnostic comparisons demonstrate that the local metallic thermal-bridge mechanism of the 3.8 mm (9-gauge) galvanized steel truss ties relative to the 50 mm concrete wythes is well captured, whereas the bulk through-wall thermal response of the assembly as a whole is systematically lagging by +13 min. Specifically, under Modeling Standard rev 4 §6, if the tie geometry had been homogenized or if the tie-concrete interface mesh (refined to level L7 at 0.03125 m = 31.25 mm across 4,016,420 cells with 87,182 metal tie cells in log.snappyHexMesh_20251009.txt) had failed to resolve the conductive bridge, the single-point peak would have collapsed toward the 9-point mean—shrinking both the 45 min lead time and the 85 °C temperature elevation at governance. Instead, the simulation reproduces the 45 min separation exactly (176 min − 131 min = 45 min) and produces a 91.2 °C (91 °C) hot-spot elevation above the 9-point mean at 131 min (slightly sharper by 6.2 °C [6 °C] than the 85 °C test contrast because the simulated bulk mean rise at governance is 89.9 °C [90 °C] vs. 96 °C in the test; note also that at t = 118 min in the run, T_unexposed_max_C = 181.6 °C sits 86.0 °C above T_unexposed_avg_C = 95.6 °C). Because both the tie-driven single-point criterion and the bulk-concrete 9-point average criterion arrive +13 min late, the error is a common-mode through-wall heat-transfer lag across the entire assembly rather than a missing tie-bridge resolution.
[P34] Where the Rework Belongs: Rework belongs in the conjugate heat-transfer (CHT) solid thermophysical property inputs and boundary/cavity heat-transfer coupling (Modeling Standard rev 4 §§3.4, 3.5, and 6; CFDME-QA-VAL-002 §8), not in re-meshing the OAS-WUI-01_revC geometry or altering D: (1) replacing any constant-property solid shortcuts (k = 1.4 W/(m·K), ρ = 2200 kg/m³, c_p = 900 J/(kg·K) nominal values in Modeling Standard rev 4 Appendix A) with full temperature-tabulated functions k(T), ρ(T), and c_p(T) for cured 28-day printed siliceous-aggregate concrete and galvanized steel across the 21.0 °C to 1050 °C E119 range per Modeling Standard rev 4 §3.5; and (2) auditing the exposed-face furnace radiative/convective boundary coupling, fvDOM cavity radiation (grey diffuse surface emissivities ε = 0.90 [dimensionless] for printed concrete and ε = 0.25 [dimensionless] for galvanized steel across the 205 mm cavity), natural-convection heat transfer in the 205 mm air gap, unexposed-face convective/radiative loss coefficients, and tie-to-concrete embedment interface conductance across the 25 mm embedment zones.

I have prepared and delivered the Section 7 Validation Memorandum as a Microsoft Word document at:

- **Deliverable Path**: `/app/files/output/CFDME-2025-041_validation_memo_revA.docx` (leaving all existing files on the file server as of `10/10/2025` untouched).

### Summary of Key Results

1. **Assembly Conformance (`OAS-WUI-01_revC` vs. Certification of Record)**:
   - **Yes — the assembly in the companion run is the exact assembly covered by the certification.**
   - **Basis**: The companion simulation (`Validation/E119_companion_sim_results.csv`), SOW (`CFDME-2025-041-SOW-01` §2), scoping memo (`§6`), Phase 1 draft report (`§3.4–§3.5`), and mesh build log (`Case/logs/log.snappyHexMesh_20251009.txt`, built `10/09/2025` from `07:14:22 MST` to `10:26:53 MST` from `OAS-WUI-01_revC.FCStd`, exported `10/08/2025 16:42:11 MST`) all use the engineering geometry of record **`OAS-WUI-01_revC`**, which corresponds to the architectural drawing-side identifier **`OAS-WA-305mm-DW`** on `Geometry/OAS_wall_assembly_section.png`. Every dimension and material matches Ironwood Certification Memorandum `IWFPE-CERT-25-0374` (`§1.2`, `09/29/2025`) and Red Butte Test Report `RBFMT-25-0918` (`§2`, `09/24/2025`): two **`50 mm`** wet-on-wet 3D-printed siliceous-aggregate portland-cement concrete leaves (`20 mm` bead pitch, `28-day` cure), an uninsulated **`205 mm`** open-air cavity (**`305 mm`** overall wall thickness), and continuous **`9-gauge` (`3.8 mm` wire diameter)** galvanized steel truss-type wire ties spaced at **`600 mm` o.c.** vertically with **`25 mm`** embedment into each leaf (**`50 mm`** total embedment). `OAS-WUI-01_revD.FCStd` (transmitted `10/09/2025` at `16:12 MST`, adding a `610 mm` hollow parapet to reach `3355 mm` height) postdates the mesh build, is not used in the run, has no Change Order under `SOW §8`, and falls outside `IWFPE-CERT-25-0374` `§1.2`.

2. **Governing Criterion, Crossing Times, Section 7 Stub, Experimental Value ($D$), and Bianca's Figure**:
   - **Governing Criterion**: Under `ASTM E119-24 §8`, the **single-point unexposed-surface temperature-rise limit of `181 °C` (`325 °F`) above initial ambient (`21.0 °C`)**, corresponding to an absolute surface temperature of **`202.0 °C`** directly over a horizontal `3.8 mm` steel tie course (`TC-6`), is reached before the `9-point` average rise limit of `139 °C` (`250 °F`) above initial ambient (**`160.0 °C`** absolute) and therefore **governs** in both the test and the companion run.
   - **Crossing Times (to the nearest `1 min`) & Section 7 Stub**:
     - **Test (`RBFMT-25-0918` §5)**: Single-point limit crossed at **`D = 118 min`** (governs); `9-point` average limit crossed at **`163 min`**.
     - **Companion Run (`E119_companion_sim_results.csv`)**: `T_unexposed_max_C` crosses `202.0 °C` (`181.0 °C` rise) between `130 min` (`200.5 °C`) and `131 min` (`202.1 °C`) at **`S = 131 min`** to the nearest `1 min` (governs), so **the prediction `S = 131 min` in the Section 7 stub stands**. For the non-governing average criterion, `T_unexposed_avg_C` crosses `160.0 °C` (`139.0 °C` rise) between `176 min` (`159.9 °C`) and `177 min` (`160.9 °C`) at **`176 min`** to the nearest `1 min` (whereas `177 min` is the first discrete `1 min` sample that trips `160.0 °C`).
   - **Adopted Experimental Value & Disposition of Bianca's Figure (`129 min`)**: We adopt **`D = 118 min`** (`RBFMT-25-0918` `§5.3`). Bianca Rennert's client-amended figure of **`129 min`** (`20251009_Rennert_revised_burn_data.eml` / `burn_data_original_vs_revised.csv`) is **rejected / inadmissible as `D`** under `CFDME-QA-VAL-002` `§6` because it lacks all `3` required laboratory documents: (1) a formally reissued test report (`RBFMT-25-0918-R1`) signed by Red Butte's authorized signatory, (2) a traceable calibration certificate for `TC-6`, and (3) an explicit supersession clause in the reissued report.

3. **ASME V&V 20 Rollup (`S, D, E, u_val`), Acceptance Criterion, Comparisons, and Largest Qualifying Prediction**:
   - **Rollup (`CFDME-QA-VAL-002` §§3–5)**: **`S = 131 min`**, **`D = 118 min`**, **`E = S − D = +13 min`** (`+11.0 %` of `D`), **`u_val = ±9 min`** (RSS of firm defaults `u_num = ±4 min`, `u_inp = ±6 min`, `u_exp = ±5 min` $\rightarrow \sqrt{77\text{ min}^2}$, reported to the nearest `1 min` as `±9 min`; `E ± u_val = +13 min ± 9 min`).
   - **Acceptance Criterion (limit as it falls)**: `|E| ≤ 10 %` of `D` = `0.10 × 118 min` = **`11.8 min`**.
   - **Comparisons**:
     - Against the acceptance criterion: **`|E| = 13 min > 11.8 min`** (exceeds limit by **`1.2 min`**, or `11.0 %` vs. `10.0 %` of `D`) $\rightarrow$ **does not meet the acceptance criterion**.
     - Against validation uncertainty: **`|E| = 13 min > u_val = 9 min`** (exceeds `u_val` by **`4 min`**) $\rightarrow$ outside the `±9 min` scatter band and **resolved as an actionable, non-conservative model error** (`E > 0` overpredicts fire endurance by `13 min`).
   - **Largest Prediction Clearing the Criterion**: **`129.8 min`** as the limit falls (`D + 0.10 × D = 118 min + 11.8 min = 129.8 min`, with lower bound `106.2 min`; in whole minutes, **`129 min`** is the largest prediction clearing `129.8 min` with `E = +11 min ≤ 11.8 min`).

4. **Two Diagnostic Comparisons, Model Assessment, Rework Scope & Status, and Phase 1 Impact**:
   - **Comparison 1 (Minutes Separating the Two Criteria)**: **`45 min`** in the test (`163 min − 118 min = 45 min`) vs. **`45 min`** in the companion run (`176 min − 131 min = 45 min` using crossing times to the nearest `1 min`). Both criteria in the run are delayed by the exact same **`+13 min`** offset.
   - **Comparison 2 (Governing Point Above the Nine-Point Mean at Governance)**: **`85 °C`** (`85 K`) in the test at `118 min` (`181 °C` rise [`202.0 °C` abs] minus `96 °C` mean rise [`117.0 °C` abs]) vs. **`91.2 °C`** (**`91 °C`** / `91 K`) in the run at `131 min` (`181.1 °C` rise [`202.1 °C` abs] minus `89.9 °C` [`90 °C`] mean rise [`110.9 °C` abs]).
   - **What They Say About the Model & Where Rework Belongs**: Because the `45 min` lead time is reproduced exactly and the local tie-to-mean contrast (`91.2 °C` [`91 °C`] vs. `85 °C`) is well resolved, the discrete `3.8 mm` steel tie geometry and L7 (`0.03125 m = 31.25 mm`) tie-interface mesh refinement are capturing the local metallic thermal bridge correctly. The `+13 min` error is a **common-mode bulk through-wall thermal lag** across the assembly. Rework belongs in the **conjugate heat-transfer (CHT) solid thermophysical property inputs (`k(T), ρ(T), c_p(T)` for `28-day` printed siliceous-aggregate concrete and galvanized steel per `Modeling Standard rev 4 §3.5`) and exposed-face/cavity radiative-convective boundary coupling (`fvDOM` cavity radiation and natural convection across the `205 mm` air gap per `§§3.4, 6`)**.
   - **Rework Status & Phase 1 Impact**: **Zero rework has been started as of `10/10/2025`** (`E119_companion_sim_results.csv` is unchanged, no rework task exists in the manifest/budget/change-order logs, and Mulshi's `Case/` files still hold a non-compliant steady RANS setup copied from Dry Wash Aerospace). Phase 1 Report `rev B` and client launch materials cannot carry an unqualified validation claim (`CFDME-QA-VAL-002 §5`), and the CHT rework plus replacement of Mulshi's steady RANS setup with transient `fireFoam` LES + `chtMultiRegion*` must be completed before locking the `6` Sprint 2 wildfire matrix production runs (`10/20/2025`), ahead of the `10/27/2025` Red Butte confirmatory window and `11/07/2025` final report.

5. **Wildfire Claim Scope, Rating Impact of `129 min`, Stamp Language, Checklist Disposition, and Paragraph for Bianca**:
   - **Wildfire Claim Scope & Future Reporting Form**: The E119 exercise evaluates through-wall heat transfer under a monotonic compartment-furnace curve only and **does not** validate the model for the mixed-convection (`Fr = 0.92, 1.48, 2.21` on `D_char = 3.0 m`), puffing (`f = 0.87 Hz`, `Q = 30.1 MW`, `D* = 3.76 m`) Sonoran buffelgrass wildfire regime or substantiate comparative claims against wood-frame construction (`CFDME-QA-VAL-002 §7`; `Modeling Standard rev 4 §7`). Closing that gap requires clearing `|E| ≤ 11.8 min` (and `≤ u_val = 9 min`) on the E119 CHT rework, aligning with the `10/27/2025` Red Butte confirmatory window, validating against wildfire-regime physical heat-flux/thermal test data, and (if comparing against wood-frame) executing a Change Order (`SOW §8`). Every future comparison must be reported in the mandatory **`S, D, E = S − D, u_val` (`E ± u_val`)** form with units—never yes/no.
   - **Rating Impact of `129 min` & Who May Act**: Because `D = 118 min` fell `2 min` short of `120 min`, Ironwood certified a **`1-hour` (`60 min`)** rating (`IWFPE-CERT-25-0374` `§3`). If `129 min` were substantiated, both criteria (`129 min` and `163 min`) would exceed `120 min`, qualifying the assembly for a **`2-hour` (`120 min`)** rating. Only **Red Butte Fire & Materials Testing (`Glen Whitfield`)** may reissue the test report (`RBFMT-25-0918-R1`) with a `TC-6` calibration certificate, and only **Ironwood Fire Protection Engineering (`Marla Kettering, PE`, AZ PE #45106)** may issue a new certification restating the rating (`IWFPE-CERT-25-0374` `§4`).
   - **Stamp Language (`CFDME-QA-VAL-002 §9`)**: `"CFD thermal analysis only. Fire-resistance rating certified separately by others."`
   - **Checklist Disposition**: This memo lets you close **Checklist Item 6** (joining **Items 1 and 8**, already closed) and settles the technical basis for **Item 7** (`OAS-WUI-01_revC` confirmed against `10/08/2025` SOW and `10/09/2025 07:14:22 MST` mesh log; `revD` excluded), while **Items 2, 3, 4, 5, 7 (pending report/case record update), 9, and 10 stay open**. Section 8 of the memo provides a ready-to-send paragraph for Bianca Rennert today.
